_comment: Geometry and feel of the 3D carousel in components/media-gallery.tsx. Everything here is a number you can turn without touching the component. The ring itself is not stored: its radius is DERIVED from the card width and how many cards are on screen (see radiusFor in the component), because a fixed radius would either overlap the cards when there are many or leave a gap when there are few. What the media IS lives in lib/media.ts; this file is only how it moves.

card._comment: Card footprint in px. Height is shared by every card - they all sit on the same rim, so a card of a different height would ride above or below the ring. Widths may differ: what the circle actually needs is even ANGULAR spacing, and a radius wide enough for the widest card. The mobile pair is used below the `mobileBelow` width.
card._borderWidth: The card's border, in px. Lives here rather than only in the CSS because the video width is derived from the space inside it; globals.css reads it back as --gal-card-border so the two can't drift.
card._labelHeight: Fixed height of the strip under the picture, in px, shared by every card. Fixed rather than free because the video width below is derived from what's left over, and a label that grew with a long title would change the shape of the video window.
card._videoAspect: The shape of the video WINDOW - the picture area, not the whole card. The card height is shared across the ring, so this is honoured by working out the width: window height x this ratio. At 16/9 a video poster is shown whole rather than cropped to fit an upright card. Widening it widens the whole ring, since the radius follows the widest card.
card._gap: Chord multiplier: 1 packs cards edge to edge, higher pushes the ring wider and opens daylight between them.

stage._comment: perspective is the viewer's distance from the front of the ring: lower is a wider, more dramatic lens. tilt is how many degrees you look DOWN at the ring, the way you look down at a round table - so the far side of the circle sits ABOVE the near side, which is what makes it read as a carousel rather than a row. Keep it shallow; past about 10 the ring stops looking like a circle and starts looking like a floor. The component applies it as rotateX(-tilt).

depth._comment: How the far side of the ring recedes. Each is applied in proportion to how far a card has turned away from the front, 0 at dead centre and 1 at the back. fade is how much opacity is lost, scrim is how much darkness is laid over, blur is in px. The backs stay visible on purpose - seeing the whole circle is the point of the thing.

motion._comment: snapMs is the glide to the next card. dragDegreesPerPx converts a drag into rotation; raise it to make the ring spin more freely under the finger. flickFactor is how far a fast flick throws the ring past where it was released.
